place.zh: 银叶谷 · 石洞 · 夜
place.en: The Silver-leaf Vale · a cave · night

setup.zh: 崖壁下一个浅石洞。你生起一小堆火挡在洞口，怀里是{伴}的鸡蛋和娘的半块饼。
setup.en: A shallow cave under the cliff. You light a small fire across its mouth; inside your jacket are {伴}'s egg and half of Mother's bread.

recap.zh: 石洞里生了火，你把吃的分给它，给它擦伤口；睡着前，有人说：本王记住你了。
recap.en: In the cave you lit a fire, shared your food with the fox and cleaned its wounds; as you fell asleep someone said: this king will remember you.

zh: 怀里两样东西：一个鸡蛋，半块饼。
en: A shallow cave, a small fire.
The resin crackles; no beast comes near.
Two things in your jacket: an egg, half a bread.

story.zh:
你在崖壁底下，找到了一个浅浅的石洞。

你先往里扔了一块石头，听了听——空的。

你又扔了一块，又听了听——还是空的。

你又捡起了第三块——

算了。你进去了。

你用你爹教的法子，拿干苔和松脂生了一小堆火。火堆挡在洞口，野兽不敢进来。

然后你从怀里，摸出了两样东西。

{伴}给的煮鸡蛋。和你娘给的那张厚饼——你家，最后的一点白面。
story.en:
Under the cliff you find a shallow cave.

First you throw a stone inside and listen — empty.

You throw another and listen again — still empty.

You pick up a third —

Forget it. You go in.

The way your father taught you, you make a small fire of dry moss and pine resin. The fire sits across the cave mouth; no beast will come in past it.

Then you take two things out of your jacket.

The boiled egg {伴} gave you. And the thick flatbread your mother gave you — the last of your family's white flour.

exits.means: shares the egg and the bread with the fox, feeds it

story.zh:
你把鸡蛋剥了，掰了一半，放在它嘴边。

它闻了闻。看了你一眼。吃了。

你想了想，把另一半也放在了它嘴边。

它闻了闻。看了你一眼。又吃了。

（{伴}，对不起。这个鸡蛋的利息，我可能要还三个了。）

然后是饼。你把饼掰成两半，一半给它，一半自己拿着。你饿了一整天，那半张饼在你手里，重得像一块金子。

它把它那一半吃完了。然后，它看着你手里的这一半。

又看了你一眼。

你看着它。它看着你。火堆噼啪响了一声。

你把你那一半，掰下来一大块，放在它嘴边。剩下一个小角，你包好，塞进了包袱最底下——明天早上的早饭。

它吃完了，舔了舔嘴。然后把脑袋一扭，闭上了眼睛。

连个谢字都没有。

你撕下衣摆，蘸着雨水，一点一点地给它擦伤口上的泥。它不咬你了。只是在你碰到疼的地方时，耳朵往后一压，小小地「呜」一声。

火光里，你看见它的伤口，在慢慢地、慢慢地合拢。

你太累了。你抱着它，靠着石壁，不知道什么时候，就睡着了。

睡着之前，你好像听见，有人在你耳边，用很小很小的声音，说了一句话。

不是狐狸叫。是人话。是一个姑娘的声音，带着一点不情不愿：

⟪「……凡人。本王记住你了。」⟫
story.en:
You peel the egg, break off half, and hold it to its mouth.

It sniffs. Looks at you. Eats it.

You think about it, and hold out the other half too.

It sniffs. Looks at you. Eats that too.

({伴}, sorry. The interest on this egg might be three now.)

Then the bread. You break it in two — half for it, half for you. You've been hungry all day, and that half a flatbread in your hand is heavy as a lump of gold.

It finishes its half. Then it looks at the half in your hand.

Then it looks at you.

You look at it. It looks at you. The fire gives a crackle.

You break a big piece off your half and hold it to its mouth. The little corner that's left, you wrap up and push to the very bottom of your bundle — tomorrow's breakfast.

It finishes, licks its lips. Then it turns its head away and shuts its eyes.

Not so much as a thank-you.

You tear a strip off your hem, wet it with rain, and wipe the mud from its wounds bit by bit. It doesn't bite you now. Only when you touch a sore spot its ears flatten, and it gives a tiny "wu."

In the firelight you see its wounds closing, slowly, slowly.

You're so tired. Holding it, leaning against the rock, you fall asleep without knowing when.

Just before sleep, you seem to hear someone say something close to your ear, very, very quietly.

Not a fox's cry. Words. A girl's voice, a little grudging:

⟪"…Mortal. This king will remember you."⟫

exits.means: keeps the food, eats it alone

story.zh:
你把鸡蛋剥了，自己吃了。

饼，你掰下一大半，也塞进了嘴里。剩下一个小角，你包好，塞进了包袱最底下——明天早上的早饭。

（这不叫小气。这叫算账。你饿了一整天。明天还不知道有没有吃的。）

它在你的衣裳里看着你。一直看着。没出声。

你被看得有点心虚，撕下衣摆，蘸着雨水，一点一点地给它擦伤口上的泥。它不咬你了。只是在你碰到疼的地方时，耳朵往后一压。

你太累了。你抱着它，靠着石壁，不知道什么时候，就睡着了。

睡着之前，你好像听见，有人在你耳边，用很小很小的声音，说了一句话。是一个姑娘的声音，带着一点不情不愿：

⟪「……凡人。小气。——本王记住你了。」⟫
story.en:
You peel the egg and eat it yourself.

The bread — you break off the bigger part and stuff that in your mouth too. The little corner that's left, you wrap up and push to the very bottom of your bundle — tomorrow's breakfast.

(This isn't stingy. This is accounting. You've been hungry all day. Who knows if there'll be food tomorrow.)

From inside your jacket it watches you. Keeps watching. Doesn't make a sound.

Feeling a bit guilty under that stare, you tear a strip off your hem, wet it with rain, and wipe the mud from its wounds bit by bit. It doesn't bite you now. Only when you touch a sore spot, its ears flatten.

You're so tired. Holding it, leaning against the rock, you fall asleep without knowing when.

Just before sleep, you seem to hear someone say something close to your ear, very, very quietly. A girl's voice, a little grudging:

⟪"…Mortal. Stingy. — This king will remember you."⟫
